hints.title: Subsequence Palindrome Expansion Obstacle
hints.text: Finding the longest palindromic subsequence requires deciding whether endpoints s[i] and s[j] match. How can comparing outer characters shrink the substring interval toward inner subproblems?

hints.title: Interval Boundary Match Invariant
hints.text: If s[i] == s[j], the longest palindrome length on interval [i, j] is 2 + length on [i + 1, j - 1]. Otherwise, it is the maximum between [i + 1, j] and [i, j - 1].

hints.title: Interval Length Bottom-Up Procedure
hints.text: Initialize a 1D array of size n with 1s. Traverse starting index i backward from n - 1 down to 0, maintaining a diagonal variable storing previous subproblem [i + 1, j - 1]. For j from i + 1 to n - 1, if s[i] == s[j], set entry j to diagonal + 2; otherwise set entry j to max(entry j, entry j - 1). Return entry n - 1.

hints.title: Complete Implementation

complexity.notes: Iterates through all substring intervals with 1D space compression.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: 1D array of length N stores interval values instead of an N x N matrix.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Using interval shrinking or LCS of s and reversed s.
